Therefore, without loss of generality, a blue-dyed ultrasound gel (Aquasonic 100, Parker Laboratories Inc.) was used to simulate the printing bioink and conduct the accuracy validation experiments. As illustrated in Fig. 1, to perform the experiments, the grooves of the calibration phantom were first carefully filled with the printing ultrasound gel. Next, the 3D point cloud of the calibration board was acquired using the Zivid Camera attached to the robotic manipulator. Of note, this scan was obtained when the camera had the recommended minimum distance of 300 mm to the calibration board. The obtained point cloud was then processed by the proposed measurement framework described in Section II-B to calculate the calibration board grooves thickness.
